property_observations.property: yield strength increase on cooling from 300 K to 4.2 K

evidence.section: 3.3. Temperature dependence of the yield strength
evidence.quote: In all samples the considerable increase of yield strength (1.5e2.5 times) is registered with decrease of compression temperature from 300 to 4.2 K.

property_observations.property: minimum strain hardening rate at stage 2

evidence.quote: there is a minimum with typical value of strain hardening rate of 2 e3 GPa

property_observations.property: minimum strain hardening rate at stage 2

evidence.quote: The minimal values of strain hardening rate at stage 2 for CoCrFeNiMn and CoCrFeNiMnV0.25 is 1e3 GPa ( Fig. 2)
at plastic strain of 0.04 the height of stress jumps is approximately 0.03 e0.04 GPa
size of stress jumps is approximately 0.01 e0.06 GPa at small strains and increases quite sharply up to 0.15 GPa
main deformation mechanism is sliding of full <110> dislocations in primary planes {1 1 1}
so twinning can be the main reason of observed increase of strain hardening rate with increase of stress.

splitting of full dislocations to the Shockley partials and formation of stacking faults, which is possible in fcc materials with low SFE and particularly is observed in CoCrFeNiMn [5]. In such case, interaction of dislocations with stacking faults may be responsible for the increased strain hardening [25].

mechanisms.name: dislocation pinning by hard sigma-phase particles

evidence.quote: Increase of V concentration leads to increase of size and quantity of the s-phase particles, which are located inside the fcc grains, main plasticity events still occur in fcc matrix, but additional applied stresses are required for dislocations to move around the hard s-phase particles, which leads to changes of mechanical properties.
decrease of strain temperature leads to decrease of activation volume, which indicates thermally activated plastic deformation.
